proposal: The Mandate recommends that WIC infant formula competitive bidding for state rebate contracts, under which states approve one brand, be regulated so that it does not unintentionally create monopolies, given that WIC buys about half of baby formula. It also calls for re-evaluating formula labeling rules and other regulations that unnecessarily delay the manufacture and sale of baby formula.

status_summary: On the formula-regulation side, HHS and FDA announced Operation Stork Speed on 2025-03-18, and FDA opened its first comprehensive review of infant formula nutrient requirements since 1998 with a request for information published 2025-05-14; Bloomberg Government reported on 2026-03-24 that FDA aims to propose a revised nutrient rule later in 2026, and no such proposal appeared in a Federal Register search through 2026-10-12. No FDA action on formula labeling or on rules that delay manufacture and sale was found. On the WIC bidding side, no USDA rule or guidance changing the single-supplier rebate model was found; USDA published only a correcting amendment (2025-12-17) restoring omitted bid-evaluation text of a 2023 rule, and said it expects no policy change. H.R. 5759 (introduced 2025-10-14) would have states select two lowest-price manufacturers, one primary and one secondary; GovInfo lists only the introduced version. Because the steps found are a review, a planned proposal and an introduced bill, the stage is proposed.

timeline.event: GAO reported that single-supplier WIC formula contracts saved about $1.6 billion in rebates in FY2023, modestly raised prices, and left two manufacturers holding nearly all contracts.
HHS and FDA announced Operation Stork Speed to expand options for safe, reliable and nutritious infant formula, as recounted in FDA's later request for information.
HHS announced that FDA would begin a review of infant formula nutrient requirements and increase contaminant testing, under Operation Stork Speed.
FDA published a request for information on infant formula nutrient requirements in the Federal Register.

H.R. 5759 (INFANT Act of 2025) was introduced, amending the Child Nutrition Act to define WIC formula competitive bidding as selecting the two lowest-price manufacturers, one primary and one secondary; referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce.
USDA published a correcting amendment to the 2023 Access to Baby Formula Act rule restoring omitted bid-evaluation provisions; FNS stated no policy change was expected.
Bloomberg Government reported that FDA plans to propose revised infant formula nutrient standards later in 2026.

title: Reform WIC infant formula bidding and re-evaluate formula regulations
uncertainties: The Operation Stork Speed launch date of 2025-03-18 is taken from the background of FDA's 2025-05-14 request for information; the March 2025 announcement itself was not fetched. Congress.gov blocks automated access, so H.R. 5759's action history could not be read; GovInfo shows only the introduced version, which suggests no further printed version, but committee action cannot be ruled out. A Federal Register search for infant formula documents in 2026 found no FDA nutrient proposed rule; it found a 2026-05-22 final guidance on protein efficiency ratio rat bioassay studies for new formulas, which refines rather than removes a premarket requirement and is not framed as burden reduction, and a 2026-06-24 WIC food package correction that does not touch formula or bidding. A FNS page on extension of infant formula rebate contracts (WIC PM 94-6), updated 2026-09-10 per research, was not read. The Mandate's monopoly concern is addressed by H.R. 5759 only in part, since it keeps a primary award.
